title: Unveiling the environmental impact of earthquakes in Europe

reading.level: final publisher full text plus supplementary information

classification.s4_s5_bridge: qualified repair/reconstruction-consequence to embodied-carbon bridge via economic-loss proxy
classification.s4_qualification: Damage-dependent repair or replacement of existing buildings; no explicit optimal retain-versus-demolish decision rule. Not reclaimed-material recoverability or quality/yield modelling.
classification.s5_qualification: Damage-induced embodied-carbon risk; not a full whole-life LCA.
classification.digital_twin: not demonstrated; GIS/exposure model/OpenQuake are not claimed as a digital twin

mechanism_steps.input: Regional probabilistic earthquake hazard, building typology and exposure
mechanism_steps.transform: OpenQuake event-based stochastic events and ground-motion fields
mechanism_steps.anchor: main pp5–6; p13 Data sources and integration

mechanism_steps.transform: Fragility gives conditional damage exceedance probabilities; consequence model maps damage into replacement-normalised economic loss
mechanism_steps.output: Event losses, averaged over simulation duration then divided by replacement cost to obtain AALR
mechanism_steps.anchor: main p6 Embodied-carbon seismic risk model

mechanism_steps.transform: Multiply quantities by mean A1–A3 ECF; add A4/A5 including demolition/disposal; multiply per-area factors by exposed built area
mechanism_steps.output: Structural and nonstructural replacement embodied carbon REC

mechanism_steps.input: AALR and REC separately for structural/nonstructural components
mechanism_steps.transform: Set AAECR=AALR; AAEC_asset=AALR_struct*REC_struct+AALR_nonstruct*REC_nonstruct; sum assets into location/national totals
mechanism_steps.output: Expected annual embodied emissions from damage repairs/reconstruction

mechanism_steps.transform: Paper states propagation to replacement carbon; numerical procedure/distribution family/covariance not supplied in main text or supplement

uncertainty_inventory.details: Event-based analysis of over3million earthquake scenarios; exact probability families, time-span value, correlation settings and epistemic logic trees not specified here; inherited GEM models referenced
Conditional damage exceedance and loss functions; parameter distributions and damage-state definitions are delegated to GEM/source models

uncertainty_inventory.status: quantified and stated propagated to REC
uncertainty_inventory.details: CoVs0.17–0.80; major concrete/cement/hollow-clay materials below0.35; resulting REC CoV approximately0.35. No explicit joint propagation into final AAEC distribution documented
Uncertainty explicitly not modelled; preliminary archetype gravity-load designs; seismic-design quantity increment omitted; assumed independent of geographic location
90% recovery/10% landfill assumed for C3–C4 factor; no contamination, sorting, degradation, market availability or recovered-quality distributions
AAECR=AALR, supported by illustrative component examples but not assigned a discrepancy distribution

demonstrated: Hazard intensity conditions damage probability; damage determines economic loss; loss ratio scales replacement carbon.
Replacement carbon depends on type, occupancy, structural/nonstructural material quantities and ECFs.
Exposure built area converts per-area carbon to asset totals.
not_reported: Covariance among ECFs/material quantities and seismic losses
Joint sampling of REC uncertainty with AALR
Probability of recovery or reuse conditional on damage severity
Explicit uncertainty distribution for the economic-to-carbon proxy
Numerical error or confidence interval on continental annual carbon mean

fixed_assumptions.value: Contemporary improved building type generally in same material category; obsolete masonry mapped to reinforced masonry; not an optimised post-disaster choice

REC A1–A5; demolished old-building C1–C4 counted in A5.1. AAEC interpreted as recurring B3–B5 risk-driven emissions; B6–B7 excluded. ModuleD introduced conceptually but no avoided-virgin-material credit calculation demonstrated

validation.supplement_examples: Clay-brick wall4.00m×2.75m; low-code5-storey RC frame;3-storey steel office. Supplement Tables1–2 and Figs1–2.
validation.interpretation: Proxy is less accurate for minor damage because labour/services contribute costs but little carbon. Steel example has more dispersion and uses economic-input-output carbon factors, reducing independence of cost/carbon comparison. These examples are not comprehensive validation across all European types.

limitations: Economic-loss proxy is not a measured carbon-damage relation for every type; no uncertainty band for proxy error.
Repair-versus-reconstruction outcomes depend on normative replacement mapping; restoration/retrofitting alternatives not optimised.
Material quantities not probabilistic and broadly geographically invariant.
ECFs biased toward data-rich European countries and time-bound EPDs.
Fixed90% recovery may fail after disasters, where damage can prevent recycling/reuse.
Only carbon is assessed; other environmental indicators are future work.
AAEC is long-run expected risk, not actual emissions in a specific year or an annual output confidence interval.
No digital twin, sensor updating, reclaimed-material quality distributions or secondary-market modelling.

summary: Full-text supports probabilistic seismic damage/repair risk transformed into expected embodied carbon through a fixed economic-loss proxy and replacement-carbon model. It does not establish propagation of circular recovery yield or reclaimed-material quality uncertainty into LCA.
